sprints.title: Accessibility — Audit all presentations for ADA/WCAG 2.1 AA compliance
sprints.notes: Full audit of all presentation HTML files across all houses. Check: semantic HTML structure (headings hierarchy, landmarks), lang attribute, color contrast ratios (WCAG 2.1 AA minimum 4.5:1 for text, 3:1 for large text), focus indicators, keyboard navigation. Use axe-core or Lighthouse to generate baseline report. Document all violations with severity levels.

sprints.title: Accessibility — Add ARIA landmarks, roles, and labels to all presentations
sprints.notes: Add role='main', role='navigation', aria-label on sections, aria-current on active slides, aria-live regions for dynamic content (slide transitions, quiz feedback, score updates). Ensure all interactive elements (buttons, links, nav controls) have accessible names. Add aria-hidden to decorative emoji/icons.

sprints.title: Accessibility — Ensure all images and icons have alt text or aria-hidden
sprints.notes: Every needs descriptive alt text. Decorative images and emoji icons (used as visual flair) get alt='' and aria-hidden='true'. SVG icons need role='img' and aria-label or . House emblem images, category images, card art — all need meaningful alt text. Check all presentation, quiz, lab, and module pages.

sprints.title: Accessibility — Fix color contrast to meet WCAG 2.1 AA across all themes
sprints.notes: Verify all text/background combos meet 4.5:1 (normal text) or 3:1 (large text, 18px+ or 14px bold). Key areas: gray text (#888, #9CA3AF) on dark backgrounds, orange/amber text on dark gray, disabled button states, placeholder text, table cell text. Fix any failing combos. Applies to all 9 house themes.

sprints.title: Accessibility — Keyboard navigation for all interactive components
sprints.notes: All interactive elements must be reachable and operable via keyboard. Slideshow presentations: arrow keys + Tab through controls, visible focus ring on current button. Quizzes: Tab through answer options, Enter to select, visible focus on current choice. Labs: Tab through all interactive areas. Skip-to-content links on every page. No keyboard traps. Focus management on slide transitions.

sprints.title: Accessibility — Screen reader compatibility for presentations and quizzes
sprints.notes: Test with NVDA or VoiceOver. Presentations: slide content must be read in logical order, slide number announced on transition (aria-live), section headers navigable. Quizzes: questions and answer choices announced clearly, correct/incorrect feedback announced, score summary readable. Tables: proper <th> scope attributes, caption elements. Ensure hidden slides are truly hidden from screen readers (display:none not just visual).

sprints.title: Accessibility — Semantic HTML structure and heading hierarchy
sprints.notes: Ensure proper heading hierarchy (h1 → h2 → h3, no skipped levels) on every page. Use semantic elements: <header>, <main>, <nav>, <section>, <article>, <footer> instead of generic <div>. Tables must have <thead>, <tbody>, <th> with scope. Lists must use <ul>/<ol> not styled divs. Forms (quiz answers) should use <fieldset> and <legend>.

sprints.title: Accessibility — Add skip navigation and focus management
sprints.notes: Add 'Skip to main content' link at top of every page (visually hidden until focused). On slide transitions, move focus to new slide content. On quiz answer submission, move focus to feedback. On modal/overlay open, trap focus inside and return on close. Ensure back-to-top and navigation links are keyboard accessible.

sprints.title: Accessibility — Automated WCAG testing integration in EduScan
sprints.notes: Add accessibility validators to EduScan that catch regressions: missing alt text, skipped heading levels, missing aria-labels on interactive elements, color contrast violations (parse CSS variables and compute ratios), missing lang attribute, missing skip-nav link. Run as part of npm run scan:syntax pipeline so new content is checked automatically.

sprints.title: Accessibility — Reduced motion and high contrast support
sprints.notes: Add @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) to disable slide animations, hover transforms, transition effects, and any auto-playing content. Add @media (prefers-contrast: more) to increase border visibility and text contrast. Ensure no content relies solely on animation to convey meaning. Test with OS-level reduced motion and high contrast settings enabled.

sprints.title: Arena/Colosseum — Review and rebalance pacing mode time values
sprints.notes: Current pacing modes: Quick (6 rounds, 90s timer, ~15 min), Standard (10 rounds, 120s timer, ~30 min), Extended (15 rounds, 150s timer, ~50 min). Playtest each mode across multiple scenarios. Are decision windows too long or too short? Does Quick feel rushed? Does Extended drag? Collect data on average time-per-round, timeout frequency, and player feedback. Propose revised values if needed. Applies to both Arena (alpha) and Colosseum (beta).

sprints.title: Arena/Colosseum — Tune round timer per scenario difficulty
sprints.notes: Currently all scenarios share the same timer values per pacing mode. Consider per-scenario timer overrides: simpler scenarios (SCN-001 Neon Pulse) could have shorter timers, complex ICS/OT or Social Engineering scenarios could have longer decision windows. Add optional decisionTimerSeconds override at the scenario level in scenarios.js that takes precedence over the pacing mode default when present.

sprints.title: Arena/Colosseum — Add adjustable game speed setting in lobby
sprints.notes: Add a speed/difficulty slider or toggle in the lobby briefing screen that lets players adjust time pressure independently of pacing mode. Options: Relaxed (timer x1.5, no auto-skip), Normal (current behavior), Intense (timer x0.75, faster inject frequency). Store preference in localStorage. This decouples round count (pacing) from time pressure (speed), giving players more control over the experience.

sprints.title: Arena/Colosseum — Balance inject timing and frequency across pacing modes
sprints.notes: Review how injects are distributed across rounds. In Quick mode (6 rounds) injects may pile up too fast; in Extended (15 rounds) there may be dead rounds with no inject activity. Check inject trigger conditions (round-based, stage-based, random). Ensure each pacing mode has a satisfying inject cadence: steady pressure in Quick, breathing room in Extended. Adjust inject scheduling arrays in scenarios.js.

sprints.title: Arena/Colosseum — Review round-to-stage mapping for all pacing modes
sprints.notes: Each pacing mode maps rounds to attack chain stages (Recon → Weaponize → Exploit → C2 → Exfil). Quick skips C2/Exfil entirely (4-stage chain in 6 rounds). Verify: does the stage progression feel natural? Are players spending enough rounds in each stage to make meaningful decisions? Should Quick include a compressed 5-stage chain instead of 4? Should Extended add a post-breach cleanup phase? Review stageSchedule arrays in scenarios.js.

sprints.title: Arena/Colosseum — Add timer pause/extend mechanic for Consultant cards
sprints.notes: Consultant cards currently provide action bonuses but don't interact with the timer. Add a timer extension mechanic: playing a Consultant could grant +15-30 bonus seconds for the current round, reflecting the 'expert brought in to help' concept. Implement via decisionTimerBonusSeconds on the Consultant card effect (similar to how Incident Commander role already grants a timer bonus). Update resolver.js and card definitions.

sprints.title: Arena/Colosseum — Implement post-game pace analytics display
sprints.notes: After a game ends, show the player a pacing breakdown: average decision time per round, rounds where timer expired (auto-skipped), fastest/slowest decisions, time spent per attack stage. This helps players self-assess and choose a better pacing mode next time. Also useful for the dev team to collect real usage data for further balancing. Display on the post-game results screen.
